title: Steak and Ale Pie
subtitle: Braised braising steak in a dark ale gravy under a puff pastry lid
excerpt: Slow-braised beef in a thick ale gravy topped with a golden puff pastry lid. A pub classic that takes time but rewards it with deep, rich flavour.
sourceNotes: British pub steak and ale pie, combining braised braising steak with dark ale gravy under a puff pastry lid, adapted from classic gastropub methods.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the braised beef filling without the pastry. Defrost overnight, top with fresh pastry and bake.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the filling batch easily. The braise keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling the day before and refrigerate. Top with cold pastry and bake when needed.

content.text: The secret here is a slow braise that gives the beef time to become tender and the gravy time to thicken. The filling must be fully cold before the pastry lid goes on. A warm filling makes the pastry go limp before it even reaches the oven.
Dust the beef cubes in flour and season. Heat the oil in the frying pan over a high heat. Brown the beef in two batches for 3 minutes per batch. Transfer to the large saucepan.
In the same frying pan, cook the onion over a medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms for 2 minutes. Transfer to the saucepan.
Add the stout, beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, tomato puree, thyme and bay leaves to the saucepan. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook on a very low heat for 2 hours until the beef is tender and the gravy thick. Remove the thyme and bay leaves. Taste and season. Spread onto a tray and cool, then chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Spoon the cold filling into the pie dish. Cut the puff pastry to fit just over the top with a little overhang.
Brush the rim of the pie dish with beaten egg. Lay the pastry over. Press the edges to seal. Brush the top with beaten egg and cut a slit in the centre.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The pastry lid sinks into the filling.
items.cause: The filling was too warm when the pastry went on.
items.fix: Cool the filling completely and chill for at least 30 minutes before adding the pastry lid.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 2 hours.
items.cause: The heat was too high and the braise boiled rather than simmered.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low so there is barely a bubble. Cook for a further 30 minutes if needed.

items.symptom: The gravy is too thin inside the pie.
items.cause: The filling was not reduced enough before it went into the dish.
items.fix: Simmer the filling uncovered for 10 minutes after braising to thicken before cooling.
